'''''Carex echinata''''' is a species of [[Carex|sedge]] known by the common names '''star sedge''' and '''little prickly sedge'''.

==Description==
''Carex echinata'' is a tussock-forming, grasslike plant in the family [[Cyperaceae]]. It has a solid, ridged stem that may exceed {{cvt|1|m}} in height with a few thready leaves toward the base. The [[inflorescence]]s are star-shaped [[raceme|spikelets]] and are {{cvt|3|-|15|mm}} wide.

It is infected by the fungal species [[Anthracoidea|''Anthracoidea karii'']].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Taylor |first1=Stewart |last2=Smith |first2=Paul A. |date=2017-01-01 |title=Having a LAFF with Anthracoidea |url=https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/401963/1/Anthracoidea%2520v8a.docx |journal=Field Mycology |language=en |volume=18 |issue=1 |pages=5–13 |doi=10.1016/j.fldmyc.2017.01.004 |issn=1468-1641|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
This plant is native to North and Central America and parts of Eurasia; as of 2016, it had spread as far as Taiwan.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Liao |first=Chun-kuei |date=January 2016 |title=Carex echinata Murray (section Stellulatae: Cyperaceae), a newly recorded sedge in Taiwan |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/306133526 |journal=Taiwan Journal of Forest Science  |doi=10.7075/TJFS |volume=31 |issue=2 |pages=143–147}}</ref> ''Carex echinata'' is a plant of wet forests, marshes, and mountain meadows of moderate elevation. It is commonly associated with [[Sphagnum|peat bogs]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cusick |first=Allison W. |date=1996 |title=Notes on the Genus Carex (Cyperaceae) in West Virginia |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/4033870 |journal=Castanea |volume=61 |issue=2 |pages=161–167 |jstor=4033870 |issn=0008-7475}}</ref>
